Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
I did a search, but did not find an answer to this...

Is the "(discard afterward)" on Tye Cooper simply reminder text? For
example, if I have 6 cards in my hand due to having a depleted library
and I use Tye Cooper to burn a vampire, I bring a card to my hand from
my ash heap. I am not over my hand size, so normally I would not need
to discard.... unless Tye's parenthetical text is actually
instruction and not reminder text. In general, parenthetical text is
reminder text, but there is reminder text that is not in parentheses,
as well as non-reminder text that *is* in parentheses on cards.
So...?

Card Text:
Tye Cooper
Requires Giovanni
3 pool
Unique wraith with 1 life. 0 strength, 1 bleed.
Tye is immune to non-aggravated damage. He may burn a non-ready minion
as a (D) action. If that action is successful, you may move a library
card from your ash heap to your hand (discard afterward).

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Chris Berger wrote:
> I did a search, but did not find an answer to this...
>
> Is the "(discard afterward)" on Tye Cooper simply reminder text? For

Yes. It's reminder text anywhere it appears.

> example, if I have 6 cards in my hand due to having a depleted library
> and I use Tye Cooper to burn a vampire, I bring a card to my hand from
> my ash heap. I am not over my hand size, so normally I would not need
> to discard.... unless Tye's parenthetical text is actually
> instruction and not reminder text. In general, parenthetical text is
> reminder text, but there is reminder text that is not in parentheses,
> as well as non-reminder text that *is* in parentheses on cards.
> So...?

So you discard to your hand size. In this case, that means you discard 0 cards.
